comparator.name: Pharmaceutical Sciences (Farmaceutische Wetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 OER lists the compulsory components and exact credits: 60 EC in Year 1, 60 EC in Year 2, and in Year 3 two 6-EC major courses, an 18-EC Bachelorproject FAR and 30 EC of open profiling space. Zero-credit lab safety, language test and tutorials are omitted from credit-bearing components but remain requirements. The OER places Project moderne ontwikkelingen in de farmaceutische wetenschappen in Year 1, whereas the general curriculum webpage places it under Year 2; this reconstruction follows the formal OER placement. No formal graduation specializations exist under OER Article 10.2; chemistry- and biology-focused minors are optional uses of the open space. Teaching language is Dutch. External credit allocation rechecked on 2026-10-08.
components: Project moderne ontwikkelingen in de farmaceutische wetenschappen
Filosofie en geschiedenis van de natuurwetenschappen
Supervised independent pharmaceutical research, thesis and presentation.
Vrije keuzeruimte, minor or approved electives
Genuinely open first-semester profiling space; chemistry- or biology-focused minors are options, not mandatory routes.

alternatives.label: Molecular disease, pharmacology & biomedical research
alternatives.concept: The strongest defensible UCR response studies molecular and cellular disease, physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, immunity, pathology, laboratory methods and quantitative evidence. It can address how drugs act on biological targets and how effectiveness and toxicity are evaluated, but it is a biomedical related-fields programme rather than pharmaceutical chemistry or drug-synthesis training.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by molecular disease mechanisms, pharmacology, biomedical laboratory work and quantitative research. The label states those supported emphases and avoids presenting the programme as Pharmaceutical Sciences or medicinal chemistry.
progression: Life-science, brain-and-behaviour, programming, mathematics, statistics and data foundations precede physiology, biochemistry, molecular-cell biology, laboratory work, anatomy and advanced pharmacology, pathology, immunity, neuroscience and evidence synthesis. HCBGATE101 and HCBGATE102 precede every dependent biomedical or psychology course, DISGATE102 precedes advanced quantitative work, and all exact planned terms pass. Eight courses are at 300 level.

core: Molecular and cellular disease, physiology and biological drug targets
Pharmacology, drug kinetics, therapeutic effects and toxicity
Medicinal and organic chemistry, molecular synthesis and compound optimisation
Biochemical, molecular and structural laboratory research
Mathematical, statistical, modelling and computational methods
Independent pharmaceutical research and responsible science
adjacent: Chemistry-focused pharmaceutical science and drug synthesis
questions: How do medicines alter disease processes?
What goes wrong inside cells during disease?
How can drug effectiveness, breakdown and side effects be tested?

candidates.label: Medicinal chemistry, synthesis & compound optimisation
candidates.assessment: UCR has biochemistry but no cumulative organic or medicinal chemistry, synthesis practicals, compound identification, structure–activity optimisation, molecular modelling for pharmacochemists or computational pharmacochemistry. A second programme would therefore misrepresent general life science and data courses as a drug-discovery chemistry curriculum.

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme is defensible around molecular disease, pharmacology and biomedical research. It also covers the eligible biology-focused pharmaceutical direction. The remaining generator-backed chemistry-and-synthesis direction is defining but infeasible at UCR; because Alternative 2 fails, the sequential rule requires production to stop at one.

notes.text: VU Pharmaceutical Sciences is a molecular and chemical drug-development bachelor with organic and medicinal chemistry, synthesis, pharmacokinetics, bioanalysis, toxicology laboratories, modelling and an 18-EC pharmaceutical project. UCR can offer one coherent related programme in molecular disease, pharmacology and biomedical research, but it is not a Pharmaceutical Sciences or drug-discovery chemistry degree.

UCR has no organic- or medicinal-chemistry sequence, compound synthesis and identification practicals, structure–activity optimisation, pharmacochemical molecular modelling, ADME laboratory sequence or pharmaceutical research capstone. Biochemistry, Pharmacology, life-science laboratory work and data science remain bounded related contributions.
